paper.title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
paper.central_claim: Self-play SWE-RL (SSR): a single LLM agent trained by RL to inject and repair increasingly complex bugs grounded in sandboxed repositories, without human-labeled issues or tests, achieves self-improvement on SWE-bench Verified (+10.4) and SWE-Bench Pro (+7.8) and outperforms a human-data baseline.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; worker read full text incl. appendices A-E and prompt templates; no page images provided. Not scored.

rationale: 范围外：自博弈RL更新并留存的只有模型权重，生成的bug制品仅作训练课程，脚手架固定，无留存的非权重组件（A3/EVIDENCE排除项）。

evidence.quote: a single LLM agent is trained via RL in a self-play setting to inject and repair increasingly complex bugs
evidence.support_explanation: Improver is an RL-trained policy; the self-play loop updates weights.

evidence.quote: Both roles share parameters and are trained jointly with RL.
evidence.support_explanation: Injector and solver are one set of weights.

evidence.quote: We use the same LLM for bug generation and repair, where the shared policy weights are updated continuously during RL.
evidence.support_explanation: Only persistent, evaluated object is the weights.

evidence.quote: The same underlying policy LLM is jointly updated on both signals.

Through comprehensive self-play, the model itself can generate an evolving curriculum of diverse, challenging bugs that naturally reflects its online and changing policy, which static bug-generation pipelines cannot provide.
evidence.support_explanation: Generated bug artifacts are a training curriculum consumed by RL, not retained harness components.

evidence.quote: Our implementation employs the same tool-based scaffold as CWM with minor prompt adjustments, incorporating Bash and a search-replace editor.
evidence.support_explanation: Agent scaffold is fixed; no harness edit is retained.

evidence.quote: SSR achieves clear self-improvement (+10.4 and +7.8 points) and consistently outperforms the human-data baseline throughout training
evidence.support_explanation: Reported gains on SWE-bench Verified / SWE-Bench Pro (weight training).

evidence.quote: While our method demonstrates consistent self-improvements across the training steps, we acknowledge the presence of evaluation noise, typically around 2% paired standard error on SWE-bench Verified.
solver feedback provides only a slight and largely negligible advantage over the consistency baseline
evidence.support_explanation: Solve-rate frontier reward adds little over consistency-only reward.

evidence.quote: However, both the data and the environments used to train these agents, such as the issue descriptions and test cases, are heavily based on human knowledge or annotations.
We do not go beyond the second order to prevent a higher likelihood of overlapping with existing bugs.
evidence.support_explanation: Higher-order bugs capped at second order.

signatures.object: policy weights of one LLM in two roles (bug injector / solver); curriculum = generated bug artifacts (bug_inject.diff, test_weaken.diff, test_script.sh, parser, test files)
signatures.information: raw Docker repos only; injector discovers tests, builds artifact; solver sees reversed test-weakening patch as spec; execution-based consistency checks and test results
signatures.operation: inject bugs (removal / history reversion), validate by 7 execution checks, solver repairs, failed repairs become higher-order bugs (<=2nd order); RL on both roles
signatures.conditions: bug-injection reward -1 invalid / -alpha at solve rate 0 or 1 / 1-(1+alpha)s otherwise; solver +-1 on all tests passing
signatures.selection_rule_data: consistency validation as gate; solve rate over G=8 attempts
signatures.persistence: weights only (curriculum is consumed during training)
signatures.later_use: evaluation on SWE-bench Verified / Pro with natural-language issues
signatures.claimed_effect: +10.4 Verified, +7.8 Pro over start; > human-data baseline
signatures.failure_boundary: unit-test-only oracle, single model for both roles, training instability at scale; solver feedback negligible in reward ablation

gap.author_gap: Software agents trained with RL still depend on human-curated issues, tests and environments, a barrier to open-ended improvement; static synthetic bug pipelines ignore the model being trained.
gap.checked_gap: Real gap for weight-training pipelines (SWE-smith, BugPilot, SWE-RL); not a harness-level gap. Not scored.

lineage.this_paper_changes: bug injection + test weakening as the specification, trained jointly with repair

gap.stakes: scalable training data for software agents
gap.method_response: self-play RL with execution-validated bug artifacts

matches.reason: proposer and solver share weights, validity anchored by execution; boundary pattern (touches weights) - no harness-level retained component.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: generator + validity gate + learner-feedback loop <-> proposer co-trained against solver with validity anchor
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: H22 requires a validity anchor and frontier signal on a fixed held-out environment; here the anchor is execution consistency but the frontier signal is the generator's own solver attempts.

expectations.check: Validity anchor the generator cannot game?
expectations.reason: Seven execution consistency checks incl. inverse mutation testing; theoretical analysis of dominant challenger strategies in App A.

expectations.check: Frontier signal measured on a fixed held-out environment?
expectations.reason: Solve rate comes from the solver's own attempts; reward ablation shows it adds little.

expectations.check: Certification outside the loop against a static/human-data baseline?
expectations.reason: SWE-bench Verified and SWE-Bench Pro vs a human-data baseline over the training trajectory; ~2% evaluation noise acknowledged.

expectations.check: Is any non-weight harness component retained and evaluated?
expectations.reason: Only weights persist; scaffold identical to CWM; bug artifacts are training data.
